_header: FIRST-PASS RATCHET — the BEST first-pass rate each exam has ever recorded. `npm run first-pass:check` recomputes the current rate from the committed packets and REFUSES when it is lower, unless a `reasons` row names the decrease with matching from/to. Raised automatically by `--write-receipt`; lowered ONLY through a reasons row. A metric that can quietly fall is not a metric — and one that quietly RISES is not evidence, so `reasons` also carries rows naming a rise, and rows naming a rate that stayed flat while the stage it stops at moved.

reasons.reason: ROSE. The four sets that stopped at generate-react did so because the fresh mint re-derived geometry from DUMP-ROUNDED boxes — imported.kbd.root.width came back "39.92px" where the corpus spells the same measurement "39.9219px" — and generate rightly refuses a slot holding two values. The census healed it with a token prune the documented CLI has no flag for; the exam, which performs no repair, took the refusal. Fixed at the cause instead: core/mint-tokens.ts now asks the corpus what it already spells at each claimed path and carries THAT when the observation is it re-rounded (MintOptions.corpusValueAt / sameUnderDumpRounding), naming every reconciled row in the proposal report. Six leaves reconciled across helper-text/kbd/label/toggle-switch; zero conflicts remain; the census prune is now a CHECKED de-dup that REFUSES a value disagreement instead of resolving it. No exam input, packet or rule changed.

FLAT, SHAPE MOVED, and this is the finding the exam existed to produce. Every set used to die at promote on “authored alert prop dismissable: prop “dismissable” is not exactly one entry of props[]” — the committed capture record carried an `icon` prop, a `dismissable` prop and six anatomy parts that NO committed input produces (hand-written into the record by ac5e6181, back-porting c924c9c2). Those four facts now ride the authored-facts door as explicit, refusable INPUTS (the door’s new `add` operation), and the record carries only what the capture produces. All eight sets now run capture → promote → validate → generate → bundle clean and stop at mint, which is MCP-DRIVEN and not a capability this harness has (docs/31 §6). The rate is still 0/8 because a PENDING mint is not a completed chain, and it will not move until an agent drives the write and records its evidence.

ROSE, because the mint stage was DRIVEN for the first time. Nothing in the engine changed: the same chain, capture → promote → validate → generate → bundle, ran green on all 8 sets exactly as before. What changed is that `mint` stopped being a permanently-PENDING architectural note and became a stage with an operator, a procedure and evidence (docs/31 §6). An agent holding the figma-console MCP tools fetched each emitted mint/<component>.figma.js INSIDE the plugin sandbox, verified its sha256 against the hash the harness recorded for those same bytes, and evaluated it EXACTLY ONCE — no retry, no repair, no hand-edited script. `--record-mint` folds that evidence in through the exam's own writers and refuses whole on any of the ways it could lie (a forbidden file key, a dropped or added set, a script sha that is not the one the chain emitted, a minted set with no picture of it, a cell with neither an image nor a named reason, or a stage that is not PENDING — so recording can never be a retry). 5 sets WROTE to the canvas, 2 the engine SKIPPED as unchanged (its own specHash already equal to the one stamped on the canvas node, so no byte moved — they complete the chain and are deliberately NOT counted in `minted`), and 1, Divider, REFUSED BY NAME: "set/standalone shape mismatch (COMPONENT_SET vs isSet=false) — a human retires the old node". THE FINDING THIS RUN EXISTS TO REPORT, and it is not in the numerator: not one of the 8 took the CREATE path. The operator created an empty page `first-pass altitude 2026-08-25`, cleared it and made it current before every run; all 8 scripts ignored it and `newPages` was [] every time. The emitted script owns file layout — it resolves its target by ds_contracts/contractId across EVERY page and amends in place — and there is no --page flag, no file-scoping and no documented way to confine a mint to one page. In the only writable file, which already carried all 8 altitude stems, a first-pass mint can therefore only ever measure the AMEND path. 7/8 is a true statement about the documented chain and a WEAKER statement than it looks: read it beside that fact, not instead of it.
